item.title: Over 40% drop in number of new cars registered in Kerry
item.description: The number of new cars registered in Kerry dropped by over 40% in November. That’s according to figures from the Society of the Irish Motor Industry (SIMI), which shows 10 cars were registered in the month. Electric cars were the most popular car registrations, however, the engine type was down over 30% compared to previous year. item.title: Kerry Fire Service gives fire safety advice for festive season
item.description: The Kerry Fire Service is says it’s important to stay fire safe during the festive season. Senior assistant chief fire officer, James Foley, says that while Christmas is about fun and spending time with family, it also brings a higher chance of fire. He says to exercise caution as candles, cooking, open fires, and electrical devices all pose an increased risk. item.description: People are being urged not to assume that someone else has already provided all the information as the Michael Gaine investigation continues. item.title: Company behind major plans for Phoenix Cinema in Dingle intend to apply for planning permission
item.description: The company behind major plans for the historic Phoenix Cinema in Dingle has announced its intention to apply for planning permission. The cinema was bought in late 2024 by visual artist Yvonne McGuinness and her husband, Oscar-winning actor Cillian Murphy. Since then, several public meetings have been held, allowing the community to have a say in the future of the not-for-profit regional cultural centre planned for the site. item.title: Kerry County Council to salt roads tonight as frosty conditions expected
item.description: Kerry County Council will be salting roads tonight, as frosty conditions are expected. Temperatures are forecast to fall below zero overnight bringing freezing conditions. The council says it will spread salt on the county's main roads from 10.30pm to ensure safer travelling conditions on Christmas Day. Advertisement Kerry County Council is urging people to reduce their speed over the coming days and to stay safe over Christmas.

item.title: Christmas day swims in Kerry tomorrow
item.description: Christmas swims are taking place across Kerry tomorrow. Local charities are set to benefit from funds raised by all the swims. They’re starting in Portmagee at half past 10 in support of Dromid Cancer Care Support Car. Advertisement The Kenmare swims begins at 11am to in aid of the Kerry Mental Health Association At the same time Killarney swimmers will raise funds at Muckross Lake in aid of mental health charity Aware.
